profile.headline: Principal Software Engineer @ Microsoft
profile.summary:
I’m a software engineer and computational scientist specializing in high-performance  algorithms and methods development. My interests primarily lie at the intersection of mixed quantum-classical software development, accelerated computing, computational physics, and numerical linear algebra. Currently, I am a Principal Quantum Software Architect at Microsoft Quantum.

Over the years, I’ve architected and/or contributed to a number of computational chemistry software packages, including NWChemEx, Chronus Quantum (ChronusQ), Psi4, Massively Parallel Quantum Chemistry (MPQC) and Gaussian. I’ve also developed a number of open-source computational chemistry libraries providing reusable software components, including GauXC, ExchCXX, IntegratorXX, and MACIS. 

From 2018-2024, I was a Scientist in the Applied Computing for Scientific Discovery Group (ACSD) of the Applied Mathematics and Computational Research Division (AMCR) at Lawerence Berkeley National Lab (LBNL). My research at LBNL centered around the development of exascale electronic structure methods and software targeting Leadership Computing Facilities (LCF) run by the US Department of Energy. I received my Ph.D. in Chemistry at the University of Washington in 2018 in the group of Xiaosong Li. My graduate research primarily centered around methods development in the field of quantum chemistry, specifically relativistic electronic structure theory and modular response theory.


Other than research, my interests include hiking, kayaking and collecting LPs. I am also a semi-active freelance musician (before Chemistry, I was a music student) and fill in as a percussionist the area from time to time.

positions.title: Principal Quantum Software Architect
positions.description:
Engineering Lead - Quantum Applications Software at Microsoft Quantum. 

Lead Architect for QDK/Chemistry and QDK/Analytics

positions.title: Research Scientist
positions.description:
Exascale Quantum Chemistry Software:
- Development of first-in-class, open source libraries for accelerated DFT simulations (GauXC, ExchCXX, IntegratorXX). These software components have seen wide adoption by the community and are well on their way to becoming the industry standard.
- Research into performance portability of quantum chemistry software targeting NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel GPUs.
- Development of the NWChemEx software package (Exascale Computing Project)
- Development of the open source MACIS library for massively parallel selected CI calculations, deployment on DOE LCF resources.
- Contributed to the strategic DOE mission for open standards and HPC software devlopment in quantum chemistry.

positions.title: Postdoctoral Research Fellow
positions.description:
Applied Mathematics Research: 
- Developed massively parallel algorithms for the solution of nonlinear eigenvalue problems on DOE LCF HPC resources. 
- Development of Krylov algorithms targeting accelerator (GPU) architectures.

positions.title: Graduate Research Assistant
positions.description: Full stack development of quantum chemistry software: brought the Chronus Quantum (ChronusQ) software package from concept to deployment. ChronusQ is now an industry standard for relativistic and time-dependent electronic structure calculations.

positions.title: Undergraduate Research Assistant
positions.description: Bioinformatics research: in silico elucidation of structure-reactivity relationships via prediction of titration curves with THEMATICS
